chains.title: Null: no TF-mediated effect of rs13078086 (passenger / linked variant)
predictions: No allele-specific reporter activity for the 200 bp window around chr3:191441666 in HCT 116 or other colorectal lines.
No allele-specific accessibility or TF ChIP/CUT&RUN signal at the exact position in HCT 116 or colon tissue; consistent with E19 (no TFAP2A peak) and E03 (no cCRE overlap).
No colon eQTL for PYDC2, PYDC2-AS1 or CCDC50 (consistent with E18), and no GWAS/Open Targets record (E04, E05).
Single-base editing of rs13078086 in HCT 116 changes no neighbouring gene by more than assay noise; any true signal in the locus maps to a different, linked base.
falsified_if: A reproducible allele-specific reporter, ATAC or ChIP difference is shown at this exact position in a colorectal context.
A colon eQTL or a credible-set GWAS association for rs13078086 emerges.
Prime-edited T>G clones show a reproducible expression change in a nearby gene.

chains.title: Ref allele binds AP-2 (TFAP2E) more; alt reduces AP-2 input to the nearby element
chains.element: Sequence 42 bp from distal enhancer-like cCRE EH38E2269392

links.claim: All four AP-2 models in group G030 agree that the T (ref) allele binds more (best model TFAP2E own model, z -18.37, effect -0.765; TFAP2A z -16.2). Within the group TFAP2E is named because it has both the best-scoring model and the highest expression in this context (8.5 TPM vs TFAP2A 6.18, TFAP2C 2.59, TFAP2B 0); the earlier TFAP2A choice rested on prior knowledge, not evidence. Caveat: both alleles sit near the 99.6-99.7th k-mer percentile, so the predicted occupancy change is small despite the large z.
The variant lies outside any cCRE, 42 bp from dELS EH38E2269392, whose signal is a maximum across biosamples; no colon- or HCT 116-specific chromatin evidence is available.

PYDC2 is taken as the candidate on proximity (19.5 kb) and on being listed for the cCRE; CCDC50 is deprioritised because it is further (112.6 kb) and shows no dependency in bowel lines, and no eQTL supports either.

TFAP2E and TFAP2A are expressed in the HCT 116 context, so AP-2 input is possible; however, no ENCODE TFAP2A peak contains the variant, which weakens the case (though no TFAP2A experiment may exist in colorectal biosamples).
No phenotype evidence: the site is not conserved (GERP -1.82), and there is no GWAS or Open Targets association, so any disease contribution would be negligible.

predictions: TFAP2E/TFAP2A CUT&RUN in HCT 116 shows a peak overlapping the variant with T-allele preference.
AP-2 (TFAP2E + TFAP2A) depletion abolishes the allelic reporter difference.
Direction is opposite to H2: T allele gives higher activity than G.
falsified_if: No AP-2 occupancy at this locus in colorectal or epithelial ChIP/CUT&RUN data (E19 already shows no TFAP2A peak).
Allelic reporter difference persists after AP-2 depletion.

chains.title: Alt allele creates a ZNF696 site in a weak distal element near PYDC2/PYDC2-AS1
chains.element: Intron of PYDC2-AS1, 42 bp from dELS EH38E2269392

links.claim: QBiC-SELEX predicts the G (alt) allele binds ZNF696 much more strongly (own model, z 23.6, effect +0.733), with the site moving from the 56.3rd to the 99.2nd k-mer percentile; group G570 contains only ZNF696, so no within-group TF choice is needed. This is in vitro prediction only, with no ChIP or allelic assay.

The variant overlaps no cCRE; the only regulatory annotation nearby is dELS EH38E2269392 42 bp away, whose DNase/H3K27ac z-scores are maxima over all biosamples, not colon-specific. Element involvement is therefore assumed, not shown.

Target is assigned by proximity only: PYDC2 is the nearest protein-coding gene (19.5 kb) and is among the genes listed for EH38E2269392; no enhancer-gene link, eQTL (E18 shows none) or perturbation evidence supports it.
ZNF696 is expressed at 8.26 TPM in the DepMap HCT 116 context used for the screen, so the created site could be bound there; no chromatin evidence for activity at this locus in colon.
No phenotype support: there is no GWAS or Open Targets record for the variant and no literature tying PYDC2 to colorectal cancer; any effect would have to be very small.

predictions: ZNF696 CUT&RUN in HCT 116 shows G-allele-preferential signal at chr3:191441666.
Allelic reporter difference (G > T or G < T) is abolished by ZNF696 knockout.
Prime-edited G/G clones shift PYDC2 or PYDC2-AS1 expression, not CCDC50.
falsified_if: No ZNF696 occupancy at this locus in colorectal cells.
ZNF696 knockout leaves any allelic reporter difference intact.
Allele-edited clones show no change in PYDC2/PYDC2-AS1.

chains.title: Ref allele binds RFX5 more; alt weakens an RFX5-dependent site near PYDC2-AS1
chains.element: PYDC2-AS1 intronic sequence adjacent to dELS EH38E2269392

links.claim: QBiC-SELEX predicts the T (ref) allele binds RFX5 more strongly (own model, z -11.73, effect -1.452); within group G094 RFX5 rather than RFX7 is named because only the RFX5 model passes and RFX5 is well expressed (20.42 TPM). The percentile shift is small (99.3rd to 98.5th), and the separate RFX2 group (E13) is not evidence for RFX5.
No cCRE overlaps the variant; the nearest dELS is 42 bp away, so the existence of an RFX-dependent element here is an assumption with no supporting chromatin evidence.
The variant lies in a PYDC2-AS1 intron, making that non-coding transcript the most proximal candidate; no eQTL or enhancer-gene link supports any target.
RFX5 is expressed at 20.42 TPM in the HCT 116 context, so the TF is present; locus activity in colon is unknown.
No evidence connects this locus or PYDC2-AS1 to colorectal cancer; the E06 hits are about other pyroptosis genes and there is no GWAS or Open Targets record.

predictions: RFX5 ChIP/CUT&RUN shows T-allele-preferential signal at the variant.
RFX5 knockdown reduces reporter activity for the T but not the G construct.
Direction: T allele gives higher element activity than G.
falsified_if: No RFX5 occupancy at the locus in colorectal cells.
Allelic reporter difference persists after RFX5 depletion, or runs in the opposite direction.

grades_v0.reason: E09 gives only an in vitro QBiC-SELEX prediction for ZNF696 (z 23.6, alt binds more). The TPM of 8.26 is not shown to be for HCT 116 in this evidence, and there is no ChIP or allelic assay.

The variant does not overlap any cCRE (E03). The nearest dELS is 42 bp away, with modest DNase and H3K27ac maxima over all biosamples. This is context only, with no evidence that the variant acts through this element.

E03 lists AC073365.1, PYDC2 and CCDC50 only as nearby genes, with no enhancer-gene link, eQTL or CRISPR data. Choosing CCDC50 (112.6 kb) over the nearer PYDC2 (19.5 kb) has no stated basis. The 'broadly expressed' claim is not backed by any cited evidence.
ZNF696 TPM is given for the HCT 116 context (E07), so expression is consistent. There is no evidence of colonic epithelial relevance or of chromatin state in HCT 116.
E04 and E05 show no association. Nothing links CCDC50 to colorectal cancer, and the E06 hits do not support it. The claim itself concedes it lacks support.

RFX5 z -11.73 with the ref allele binding more is a direction-consistent QBiC-SELEX prediction only (E15). The ref site is already at the 99.3rd percentile, so the change is modest. RFX2 group (E13) is a different TF and adds no support for RFX5.
The claim itself says the site lies outside the dELS. 'RFX5 commonly occupies X-box elements' comes from memory, not from cited evidence. Nothing supports an RFX-dependent element here.
PYDC2 is chosen only by proximity (E02). There is no cCRE-gene link, eQTL or perturbation evidence. PYDC2-AS1 is also an intron host, but nothing ties it to regulation.
RFX5 at 20.42 TPM (E15) shows the TF is expressed. Nothing shows the locus is active in HCT 116 or colon.
The claim itself says that no study ties PYDC2 to colorectal cancer risk. The E06 hits are not specific to PYDC2 and colorectal cancer, and E04 shows no association.

All four AP-2 models agree on the direction (E10), but this is a prediction only. Both ref and alt sit at about the 99.6-99.7th percentile, so the change is small despite the large z. TFAP2A was chosen over the higher-expressed TFAP2E on 'well-characterized' grounds, not on evidence.
The cCRE is 42 bp away and does not overlap the variant (E03). The claim that the site is 'genuine' rests on k-mer percentile alone.
CCDC50 is chosen with no enhancer-gene, eQTL or perturbation evidence (E02, E03). Being 'likeliest expressed' is not shown.
TFAP2A (6.18 TPM) and TFAP2E (8.5 TPM) are expressed in the context (E10). This shows expression only, not that the locus is active there.
The claim cites E01, E04 and E05, none of which supports a link to colorectal cancer. GERP is -1.82, which argues against function. No gene-disease evidence is cited.

The Ets group disagrees on direction (E12), and ETV5 has only a small effect (0.251), so any binding effect is unreliable. The chain's tf (ETV5) is picked as 'best-scoring' with no reason beyond that. It also argues that the causal variant is elsewhere.
The nearby dELS is 42 bp away and does not overlap (E03). No evidence for a linked causal variant is cited, and no LD data are provided.
Nothing ties any variant in the element to CCDC50 or PYDC2. The claim 'would act on' is speculation (E02, E03).
The Ets TPM values (E12) show the factors are expressed, which is consistent with the claim. There is no chromatin or cell-type evidence for the locus.
No association exists (E04, E05), so there is nothing for an LD tag to explain. The chain is untestable with the provided evidence.

grades_final.reason: E09 gives a QBiC-SELEX prediction only (own ZNF696 model, z 23.6, alt binds more). The group contains only ZNF696, so there is no TF-choice problem. There is no ChIP or allelic assay, so a binding prediction alone is at best weak.

E03 shows no cCRE overlaps the variant. The nearest dELS is 42 bp away, with maximum-over-biosample z-scores. The chain itself says element involvement is assumed. Nothing cited shows the variant lies in an active element.
PYDC2 is assigned by proximity only (E02, E03 nearby-gene list). E18 shows no eQTL and there is no perturbation or enhancer-gene link. This is consistent with the claim but indirect.
ZNF696 is expressed at 8.26 TPM in HCT 116 (E09). Expression context only, with no chromatin or occupancy evidence at this locus in colon.
E04 and E05 show no GWAS or Open Targets association. The E06 hits do not tie PYDC2 to colorectal cancer. Nothing cited supports a phenotype link.

E15 gives a QBiC-SELEX prediction only (RFX5 own model, z -11.73, ref binds more). RFX5 is the only passing member, so the TF choice is justified. The percentile shift is small (99.3 to 98.5) and there is no ChIP or allelic assay.
E03 shows no cCRE overlaps the variant. The nearest dELS is 42 bp away. No chromatin evidence supports an RFX-dependent element, and the chain admits it is an assumption.
E01 places the variant in a PYDC2-AS1 intron, so the transcript is proximal. E18 shows no eQTL and there is no enhancer-gene link. Proximity only, so it is consistent but indirect.
RFX5 is expressed at 20.42 TPM (E15), so the TF is present. There is no evidence of locus activity or occupancy in HCT 116 or colon.
E04 and E05 show no association. The E06 hits concern other pyroptosis genes. Nothing links PYDC2-AS1 or the locus to colorectal cancer.

E10 gives a QBiC-SELEX prediction only. All four AP-2 models agree that ref binds more, and TFAP2E is chosen on stated grounds (best model, highest expression). Both alleles sit near the 99.6-99.7th percentile, so the occupancy change is small, and there is no ChIP. E19 shows no TFAP2A peak.
E03 shows no cCRE overlaps the variant. The nearest dELS is 42 bp away with biosample-maximum signal. There is no colon-specific chromatin evidence.

PYDC2 is chosen by proximity and the cCRE gene list (E02, E03). E18 shows no eQTL. E20 shows CCDC50 is not a dependency, but that does not bear on regulation by this variant. This is indirect and non-specific.
TFAP2E and TFAP2A are expressed in the HCT 116 context (E10). E19 shows no TFAP2A peak at the variant, though the absence is ambiguous. Expression alone gives only weak support.
E04 and E05 show no association, and GERP is -1.82 (E01), so the site is not conserved. Nothing supports a phenotype link.

checks.why: An eQTL for CCDC50 or PYDC2 would tie the variant to a gene, and would also distinguish the null from the gene links of H2, H3 and H4.
Tests whether an AP-2 peak overlaps the variant in a colorectal line, which is the only empirical binding check available for H4.
Tests whether CCDC50 has any relevance to colorectal cancer cell fitness, which would bear on the phenotype link.
